# App options

The config keys of the app itself, its name, public URL, secret, language, time zone, install colours and mobile build, with their types, defaults and environment variables.

The keys of the app itself, at the top level of [`protobase.config.ts`](../config.md).

## name

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `Protobase`
- **Environment variable:** `PROTOBASE_APP_NAME`, which overrides it

The app's name: sign-in prompts and passkeys show it, the mail it sends names the app with it and is sent as it, and the sidebar, the browser tabs and the [installed app](../installable-app.md) are called by it. A deployment renames the app with `PROTOBASE_APP_NAME`, which wins over the config. The name reaches the app through its sign-in, so with sign-in off (`auth: false`, or an `authenticate.jwksUrl` without `auth`) the app shows `PROTOBASE_APP_NAME`, else `Protobase`, and only [`protobase mobile`](../cli.md#mobile) reads `name` itself. See [App identity](../app-identity.md#the-name).

```ts
export default defineConfig({ name: 'Property Finder' })
```

## url

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `PROTOBASE_URL`; in `protobase dev`, the dev server's own address
- **Environment variable:** `PROTOBASE_URL`

The app's public URL: the issuer and audience of its tokens, and where its emails link to. Sign-in needs it: with `auth` on, `protobase dev`, `serve` and the commands that sign people in stop with a clear message when it is missing. Other origins the app is served on are [`auth.origins`](sign-in.md#authorigins).

```ts
export default defineConfig({ url: 'https://admin.example.com' })
```

## secret

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `PROTOBASE_SECRET`
- **Environment variable:** `PROTOBASE_SECRET`

The app's secret, made with `openssl rand -base64 32`: it signs session cookies, upload tickets, download links and public forms' bot checks, and encrypts the token signing keys. Sign-in needs it, and file fields too unless [`files.secret`](files.md#filessecret) names another; public forms sign their bot checks with `PROTOBASE_FORMS_SECRET` instead when it is set. Keep it out of the config's source and read it from the environment, which the default does.

```ts
export default defineConfig(({ env }) => ({ secret: env.ADMIN_SECRET }))
```

## previousSecrets

- **Type:** `string[]`
- **Default:** `PROTOBASE_PREVIOUS_SECRETS`, comma separated; none
- **Environment variable:** `PROTOBASE_PREVIOUS_SECRETS`

The app's secrets before `secret`, newest first. The app encrypts with `secret` and still decrypts what these encrypted, so after the secret changes the token signing keys keep signing and the tokens in flight keep verifying. Keep an old secret listed until the keys it encrypted have rotated out ([`signingKeyDays`](sign-in.md#signingkeydays)), and while authenticator apps set up before the change are in use. See [Changing the secret](../auth.md#changing-the-secret).

```ts
export default defineConfig(({ env }) => ({ secret: env.ADMIN_SECRET, previousSecrets: [env.OLD_ADMIN_SECRET] }))
```

## locale

- **Type:** `'en' | 'nl'`
- **Default:** each user's browser's language, when the screens come in it; English otherwise

The language of the admin app's built-in screens and of its numbers and dates, for every user. Any other value stops the app at start. See [Languages](../languages.md).

```ts
export default defineConfig({ locale: 'nl' })
```

## timezone

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `UTC`

The time zone the jobs' schedules are read in, such as `Europe/Amsterdam`, unless a job names its own [`timezone`](jobs-and-events.md#jobs). See [Recurring jobs](../jobs.md#recurring-jobs).

```ts
export default defineConfig({ timezone: 'Europe/Amsterdam' })
```

## themeColor

- **Type:** `string`, any CSS colour

The colour of the installed app's title bar and of the browser's toolbar around it, the web manifest's `theme_color`. See [App identity](../app-identity.md#the-colours).

```ts
export default defineConfig({ themeColor: '#0d9488' })
```

## backgroundColor

- **Type:** `string`, any CSS colour

The colour of the screen the installed app shows while it starts, the web manifest's `background_color`.

```ts
export default defineConfig({ backgroundColor: '#ffffff' })
```

## mobile

- **Type:** `{ appId: string; plugins?: Record<string, string> }`

The app's iOS and Android build: with it, `protobase mobile` builds the app with Capacitor, and the API also allows the app's Capacitor origins (`capacitor://localhost`, `https://localhost`) for [CORS](api.md#cors). See [A mobile app](../../guides/mobile-app.md).

- `appId`: the app's id on both iOS and Android, such as `com.example.shop`: two or more dot-separated parts, each a letter then letters and digits.
- `plugins`: extra native Capacitor plugins, by npm name and version range. A range fetched over plain `http:` or `git:` is refused.

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  mobile: { appId: 'com.example.shop', plugins: { '@capacitor/camera': '^8.0.0' } },
})
```
